title: Language Structures and Conventions
summary: Parts of speech, tenses and concord, active and passive voice, direct and indirect speech, sentence types, and punctuation.

rows: Names a person, place, thing or idea
Describes a verb, adjective or adverb

items: Singular subject, singular verb: 'The *list* of names **is** long.' (The subject is 'list', not 'names'.)
With 'either…or' / 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject: 'Neither the teacher nor the learners **were** late.'

notes.title: Tricky concord
notes.problem: Choose: 'Each of the boys (has/have) a book.'
steps: The subject is 'each', which is singular.
'Of the boys' is only a phrase.
notes.answer: 'Each of the boys has a book.'

notes.text: **Active**: the subject does the action: 'The dog chased the cat.' **Passive**: the subject receives the action: 'The cat was chased by the dog.' Keep the tense the same when changing voice.

notes.title: Changing to indirect speech
notes.problem: Sipho said, "I am going to the library today."
steps: Move the tense back: am going → was going.
Change time words: today → that day.
notes.answer: Sipho said that he was going to the library that day.

items: **Compound**: two main clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction: 'The bell rang, and we left.'
**Complex**: a main clause and a subordinate clause: 'When the bell rang, we left.'

notes.label: Punctuation
notes.text: **Apostrophe**: possession (the girl's bag, the girls' bags) and contractions (it's = it is; *its* is possessive). **Comma**: after an introductory clause and to separate list items. **Colon**: introduces a list or explanation. **Semicolon**: joins two closely related main clauses.

questions.prompt: Identify the adverb: 'The old man walked slowly to the bus stop.'
Choose the correct verb: 'The box of oranges ___ on the table.'
Choose the correct word: 'The cat licked ___ paw.'
'Everyone have finished their work' is grammatically correct.
Is this sentence simple, compound or complex? 'Although it rained, the match continued.'
Match each word class to an example.
Change to the passive voice: 'The learners painted the classroom.'
questions.memo:
✓ The classroom was painted (1)
✓ by the learners. (1)

questions.prompt: Change to indirect speech: Lerato said, "I will finish my essay tomorrow."
questions.memo:
✓ Lerato said that she (1)
✓ would finish her essay (1)
✓ the next day / the following day. (1)

questions.prompt: Correct the apostrophe errors: 'The boys' bike lost it's chain.' (one boy)
Join into one complex sentence: 'The road was flooded. We took another route.'
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'Because the road was flooded, we took another route.' (subordinating conjunction and correct punctuation) (2)
